title: ops-spark-release-atelier-checklist-and-calendar-jun-2026-sketch
content:
Purpose
---
Quick, compact operations brief for the "ops-spark" feature push (autoscaling kernel selector + short-sequence batching). This is a working sketch: mix of a checklist, a day-by-day rollout calendar, and a draft of release notes. Intended audience: release conductor, SRE on-call, serving-runtime owners, console product PM.

Goals
- Ship autoscaling kernel selector behind feature flag KERNEL_SEL=true.
- Validate end-to-end latency SLOs for 16–128 token requests across two regions (us-west1, eu-west1).
- No user-facing errors > 0.1% during staggered ramp to 100% traffic.

High-level rollout plan (calendar)
- Wed 2026-06-02: Feature freeze (code/infra). Stop merging non-critical PRs.
- Thu 2026-06-03: Canary slot A (5% traffic) in us-west1 for 2h, smoke + perf.
- Thu 2026-06-03 1800 UTC: Canary slot B (5% traffic) in eu-west1 for 2h.
- Fri 2026-06-04: Ramp to 20% in both regions across 4h window with autoscale metrics on.
- Mon 2026-06-07: Ramp to 50% after 24h observation and gating.
- Wed 2026-06-09: Full rollout to 100% subject to health gates (24h).

Day-of deploy quick checklist (preflight, hour blocks)
- 72–48h before:
  - Confirm canary tokens & secrets available in vault (Priya).
  - Ensure external partners notified (if applicable).
  - Load gen baseline snapshot updated (Luca) — attach snapshot id.
- 24h before:
  - Merge freeze verified on main branch, CI green.
  - Alerting playbook pinned to #oncall and PagerDuty escalation set.
- 2h before:
  - Run local smoke: model load, sample generation, kv-cache warmup.
  - Verify prewarm pipeline (if caching enabled).
- 15m before:
  - Hand-off readout: oncall, release conductor, serving-runtime owner, infra lead.
  - Confirm observability dashboards ok (latency P50/P90, error rate, QPS, GPU util).

Minute-by-minute (canary slot example, US-WEST)
- T0: Flip KERNEL_SEL=true for canary route via rollout manager (canary config id: canary-ops-2026-06-03-a).
- T+5m: Run canary synthetic traffic (5m spike at 2x expected qps) — run load-gen script: loadgen/canary_usw.sh.
- T+20m: Verify P90 latency and 99th percentile tail; check KV cache hit ratio.
- T+60m: Check telemetry: gc pauses, reties, 5xx spikes. If any metric breach, rollback to previous canary config and escalate.
- T+120m: If stable, promote to slot B / other region or ramp per calendar.

Roles & Contacts
- Release conductor: Maya Chen (pager: +1-555-0123, slack:@mchen)
- Serving runtime owner: Luca Romano (slack:@luca)
- Observability lead: Priya Singh (slack:@priya)
- SRE primary oncall: Samir Desai (PagerDuty: samir-sre)
- Infra lead (networking & k8s): Janelle Ortiz

Gating criteria (must pass to progress)
- Error rate (5xx) <= 0.1% sustained over 30m at canary QPS.
- P90 latency regression <= +10% vs baseline for same load-profile.
- GPU OOMs: zero. Any OOM -> immediate rollback.
- No increase in cold-starts > 2x baseline in the first 2h.

Telemetry & dashboards to watch (links pinned in CONFLUENCE-4567)
- per-route latency (p50/p90/p99) by model-size and seq-length.
- error-rate by error-class (5xx/4xx/resource).
- GPU memory pressure + kernel fallback counts.
- Autoscaler decisions: scale up/down events and reasons.
- KV cache hit/miss ratio; request-level cache effectiveness.

Rollback decision tree (simple)
1) Crash / 5xx spike > threshold -> immediate rollback of canary route.
2) Latency regression persists beyond 30m and operator investigation points to kernel selector -> rollback.
3) Intermittent errors but low volume: hold and investigate with increased sampling; patch if needed.
4) Persistent but small perf delta (<10%) acceptable if accompanied by cost reduction note and PM sign-off.

Smoke test checklist (automated + manual)
- Automated unit smoke: fast-suite on build (unit, small integration).
- E2E smoke: sample prompt generation for 16/64/128 tokens, assert shape + tokens returned.
- KV cache: warmup + re-request path (expect hit > 30% after warmup).
- Topline correctness: run 10 golden prompts, diff vs baseline for major divergence > 0.5 BLEU (note: BLEU is a rough measure; file diffs in /test/golden/).

Rollout tuning knobs (ops notes)
- Throttle curve: use three-step ramp (5% -> 20% -> 50%) with at least 30m observation at each step.
- Batching window: start with 12ms and monitor latency tail; reduce window if p99 regresses.
- Quantized variant fallback: if kernel selector chooses quantized path and perf degrades, auto-fallback to float32 path for small seq lengths.

Draft release notes (internal copy)
- Title: "Autoscaling Kernel Selector (experimental) - ops-spark"
- Short summary: Introduces an experimental kernel selector that chooses execution kernels based on sequence length distribution and current GPU memory pressure. Initial rollout will be gated behind feature flag and available in us-west1 and eu-west1.
- Why it matters: Expected median latency improvement of ~8–12% for mixed short/medium requests and potential 10–18% reduction in per-token GPU cost under heavy batching.
- Known limitations: feature is experimental; small risk of increased p99 for very long sequences; we will fall back to previous kernel on regressions.
- How to opt-in: set KERNEL_SEL=true on route-level config or use rollout manager ID canary-ops-2026-06-03-a.

Open questions / TODOs (notes-to-self)
- Add a short-run synthetic that simulates stochastic sequence lengths (currently only fixed-len loads). TODO: Luca to add by 2026-06-01.
- Confirm billing metric mapping for per-token cost change (Finance input needed) — PRIYA to loop in finance-analytics.
- Decide on post-rollout experiment length (30d vs 14d). Pro: longer gives signals on cost; Con: slower iteration. Recommend 21d.

Appendix (quick links and snippets)
- Promoted canary config: canary-ops-2026-06-03-a
- Load-gen commands: ./tools/loadgen --profile canary_usw --duration 300 --qps 600
- Quick rollback script: infra/rollbacks/rollback-route.sh canary-ops-2026-06-03-a

Notes on tone: keep this doc compact. This is a working sketch — we'll convert to the long-form runbook if the canary passes.

-- end of sketch --
